education.title: The Multibagger Entry Window
education.content:
A 2024 study by O'Shaughnessy Asset Management tracked every US stock that returned 500%+ between 2010 and 2023. The median entry point was 34% below the prior 52-week high.

Not at the bottom. Not at the top. In the recovery zone, after maximum pessimism had passed but before momentum confirmation attracted the crowd.

Our screening system targets exactly this window: structural trend reversals where institutional capital is building but the stock is still unloved. Seven of our current 13 positions were entered within 40% of their 52-week lows.

The wreckage is where the asymmetry lives.

Not financial advice.

education.title: Why the System Rejects 99.8% of Stocks
education.content:
Our last screening session loaded 1,279 stocks. Eighteen passed the initial momentum confirmation. Six survived theme quality scoring. Three cleared the final forensic audit.

That is a 99.8% rejection rate.

Most screening systems optimise for inclusion: find as many ideas as possible. Ours optimises for exclusion. Every gate is designed to eliminate, not to confirm. The technical filter removes stocks without confirmed trend reversals. The theme filter removes stocks in weak or crowded sectors. The forensic audit removes stocks with capital structure problems, management red flags, or insufficient catalysts.

The best signal the system produces is "no."

Not financial advice.

education.title: What Structural Forces Actually Mean
education.content:
Not all investment themes are equal. We classify capital flows into structural forces: multi-year spending commitments backed by government budgets, regulatory mandates, or infrastructure requirements that cannot be reversed by a single earnings miss.

Defence Spending: $1.01 trillion FY2027 budget, bipartisan support. Nuclear Renaissance: 14 SMR applications at the NRC, hyperscaler power demand. Biotech Capital Cycle: XBI up 40.8% trailing twelve months, IPO window reopened, $133B in biopharma M&A in 2025.

A force is not a narrative. It is a measurable capital flow with a multi-year runway. Our portfolio maps every position to a force. When a force weakens, positions in that force get re-evaluated regardless of individual stock performance.

Not financial advice.

education.title: The Insider Purchase Signal
education.content:
When a CEO buys shares on the open market, the average subsequent 12-month return is 11.2% above the benchmark. That finding comes from a study of 64,000 insider transactions between 2003 and 2021 published in the Journal of Financial Economics.

The key word is "open market." Grants, exercises, and 10b5-1 plan purchases carry no informational signal. Only discretionary purchases with personal capital matter.

$SVCO's CEO Walden Rhines bought $170,000 of stock at the all-time low. He previously grew Mentor Graphics from $400M to a $4.5B Siemens acquisition. When a CEO with that track record uses personal capital at a multi-year low, the information asymmetry favours the buyer.

Not financial advice.

scanner.title: The April Screening Funnel
scanner.content:
The April 13 screening session: 1,279 tickers loaded across all US exchanges.

18 passed the initial momentum confirmation. Six cleared combined filters across 15 distinct micro-themes. Three survived the forensic audit at conviction 7 or higher.

The three: $CYRX (cold chain logistics monopoly, conviction 8), $KYTX (autoimmune CAR-T first-to-market, conviction 7), $NAMS (oral CETP inhibitor, conviction 6).

All three in the Biotech Capital Cycle force. Scanner convergence in a single force is rare and informative: it means institutional capital is rotating into the sector with enough breadth to confirm the structural thesis.

99.8% eliminated. That filtering is the system working.

Not financial advice.

scanner.title: DLO: The Signal We Walked Away From
scanner.content:
DLocal processes payments for six of the Magnificent Seven across 44 emerging markets. Revenue grew 47% to $1.09 billion. Forward P/E of 14.9x versus a 39.5x fintech peer average.

Our screening system flagged it. The theme scored 7.0 out of 10. The momentum signal was confirmed.

We walked away.

No structural force alignment. The EM payment infrastructure theme lacked the multi-year government or regulatory catalyst that anchors a force. General Atlantic was selling. Take-rate compressing from 1.19% to 0.88%. Dual-class voting gave insiders 79.5% control.

The numbers looked right. The structure did not. Knowing the difference is the entire edge.

Not financial advice.

scanner.title: Theme Quality from the April Scan
scanner.content:
Themes from the April 13 scan, ranked by composite quality score:

Three rated PRIME (highest quality, active catalysts, capital flowing): navy submarine hardware manufacturing, CAR-T autoimmune first-to-market, oral CETP inhibitor regulatory filing.

Two rated INVESTABLE (viable but need better timing): CGT cold chain logistics, EM cross-border payment infrastructure.

One rated INVESTABLE on optical interconnects: the 800G ramp cycle with hyperscaler capex at $690 billion.

Eleven themes rejected below our quality threshold. Rejected themes included EV manufacturing, movie exhibition, community banking, and radio media. The scanner does not chase narrative. It scores catalyst density, momentum alignment, crowding risk, and runway.

Not financial advice.
